The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, as preemptors, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 1998 in the court of Assistant Judge, Jagannathpur, Sunamganj impleading this present petitioner and others as opposite parties seeking pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 4. The case of the preemptors, in short, was that they were co-sharers by purchase of the case holding and also holders of land contiguous to the case land. That the opposite party No. 3 sold the case land to the preemptee opposite party No. 1 by registered kabala dated 16.09.1997 beyond the knowledge of the preemptors and without serving any notice upon them under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. That the preemptee was a stranger to the case holding. That knowing about the case transfer the preemptors filed the case within the statutory period of limitation on depositing the requisite amount. 

 14. It appears that the only point which has been agitated before us from the side of the petitioners was considered deeply by all the courts below. Admittedly, the case land was agricultural land at the time of its transfer to the pre-emptee. The pre-emptee after his purchase of the case land constructed his dwelling house thereon. It appears that the High Court Division considering all these facts, circumstances and materials on record and also the judgment of the courts below opined that in this case the protection of section 6 of Land Reforms Ordinance, 1984 was of no help for the pre-emptee inasmuch as it has been well proved from the evidence including the advocate commissioner's report-exhibit-1 that the case land was agricultural land at the time of its transfer to the pre-emptee and the pre-emptee after his purchase constructed his dwelling house thereon. The High Court Division thus held that since at the time of transfer in question the case land was admittedly, agricultural land there is no bar in allowing the preemption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It appears that the High Court Division has considered also the further plea of the preempted that he has got no other homestead to live in and on analysis of the evidence found out that this plea of the pre-emptee has not been proved at all, rather from the evidence of his witnesses it has been proved that he has got his ancestral homestead and other house also.
